reviews.review: under rated but only with mods

[h2]Enormous and complex open-world sci-fi shooter. 8/10[/h2]

I'm shocked to read negative reviews, this genuinely plays better than the original Mass Effect games. I understand that it may not resonate with people who are nostalgic for Shepherd and Liara, but if you set aside any comparisons to the original trilogy, this game is phenomenal.

Some positives: the supporting characters are delightfully deep and charming, with tons of unique interactions with each other and conflicting philosophies. Combat is deep but accessible: you can delve into combos and profiles if you want, but you can also just play the game like a shooter. Crafting and the economy are perfect: rewarding you for exploring, buying, selling, foraging and scanning, but limiting your access to resources so that every new research feels special. Each planet has so much to do, and there are quite a number of them. Also, the opening sequence is long but quite narrative and thrilling. It really felt like watching a sci fi movie.

Sure there are also some negatives. Most annoying is probably Ryder's (the protagonist) personality, who could learn something from the more stoic Shepherd. There is still the occasional glitch like a trigger not opening a door or some dialogue that wrongly assumes you made a certain choice previously. Although the galaxy map is great, movement between planets is annoyingly slow, with several unskippable cutscenes. However, these are certainly not enough to hamper a very solid game.

To be clear, Andromeda doesn't have a bad storyline. It's actually quite intriguing to discover more about the Kett, the Angara, and to build up a new galactic community. And I do love the contrast Ryder provides compared to Shepherd in the original Mass Effect Trilogy. But...and this is a pretty big but...the missions and assignments feel pointless, almost like busy work, and there are SO MANY of them, so if you're a completionist or want the things you choose to do to matter, then playing becomes a senseless slog. 

I'm at about 60% complete and had to take a break from playing--which it is ridiculous to have to take a break from something that's supposed to be fun--because I'm going to lose my mind from tedium at this rate.

Additionally, the Nomad is the ABSOLUTE WORST vehicle Mass Effect has ever had. Possibly that any video game has ever had. Getting over a simple hill was so often impossible that I usually chose to risk dying in harsh conditions running to a nav point rather than spend another second trying to figure out where the wretched thing could go. This is compounded by the quest markers occasionally glitching to where you're running in circles like a mad person trying to figure out where the heck you're supposed to go (it's usually nowhere in the area the marker is leading).

If you do purchase this game,  to have the best experience I reccomend only focusing on Priority Ops, Allies and Relationships, and,some of the Heleus Assignments. Additional Tasks are worthless.
Great fun game i keep coming back for another play through
